prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / compositing.
Asset: preview revision of the Quality & Compliance page's Our Commitment photograph.

INPUTS:
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: two quality inspectors at a stainless-steel food packaging conveyor in a modern factory.
Image 2 is the exact Fonte logo artwork for the inspectors' lab coats.
Image 3 is the authoritative product reference: a sealed yellow and clear Fonte Tortilla Wraps pouch. Use ONLY that packaged product from this reference, not the kitchen, food styling, utensils or background.

PRIMARY EDIT:
Make the target look like a convincing real documentary photograph of quality assurance in a Saudi food-packaging facility, preserving the same basic scene, two foreground inspectors, workstations, factory perspective and wide 3:2 composition. Improve realism with natural human proportions, individual skin texture, believable eyes and hands, real fabric weave and folds, subtle stainless-steel texture and accurate lighting and shadows. No airbrushed skin, fake render gloss, exaggerated smiles, distorted equipment or artificial dramatic grading. Clean, professionally maintained factory with neutral realistic industrial lighting.

BRANDING:
Remove EVERY Masdar Al Hayat corporate logo, Arabic/English wordmark and identifier from the scene, including the large wall plaque, both lab coats and the paperwork/clipboard on the right-hand table. Restore the wall as a clean plain factory wall and use plain unbranded inspection paperwork. Place the supplied authentic red/white/gold Fonte logo from image 2 on the left chest of BOTH foreground white lab coats, where their existing logos were. A modest realistic approximately 6–7 cm wide sewn or embroidered patch, following the fabric perspective and folds, not a floating oversized decal. Preserve the Fonte Arabic wordmark shape and exact English spelling. Do not add other signs or wall branding.

PRODUCT:
Replace the generic green-and-white packs on the conveyor and in the right-hand inspector's hands with the SAME genuine yellow/clear Fonte Tortilla Wraps pouch from image 3. One consistent product SKU throughout. Put two sealed pouches lying naturally flat on the conveyor with their printed fronts uppermost, at sensible spacing and size, and one matching sealed pouch supported naturally in the main inspector's hands as he examines its packaging/seal. Show enough of the printed yellow front face on the held sample to recognize the product, while keeping his working gaze directed at it. Preserve the exact rectangular thin soft pouch structure, original Fonte logo, yellow artwork, transparent right-hand window revealing stacked round tortillas, printed food photograph, Arabic and English label arrangement, heat-sealed edges and realistic filled thickness. Treat the product artwork as locked photographic reference material, not a design brief: no invented brands, redesigns or mismatched colors. Ground every pouch with believable contact shadows, reflections and perspective. Do not make it into a carton or a bag of loose chips.

PEOPLE AND ACTIVITY:
Keep the two foreground men recognizable. The right-hand inspector carefully checks the sealed sample; the colleague observes and records on the plain black tablet/clipboard. Both should wear the existing white coats and hairnets plus clean fitted light-blue disposable gloves for handling the packs. Preserve believable poses, sensible hand placement and anatomically correct fingers. Keep the existing surgical mask on the left inspector; use a subtle appropriate beard cover on the right inspector if needed for the factory setting. Other workers/equipment remain softly in the background, without added focal people.

No captions, watermarks, split screens or graphic overlays. No Masdar corporate marks anywhere. Fonte branding only on the specified lab-coat patches and real product packaging. The result must feel photographed, not like a synthetic product advertisement.
